description.undefined:
The QAECY Ontology defines the core knowledge model used by QAECY and the Cue Agent to represent information from Architecture, Engineering, and Construction projects.

The model is centered around information objects and entity references. Information is represented through FileLocation, InformationObject and Fragment, while project meaning is represented through EntityMention and CanonicalEntity. Entity mentions are resolved to canonical entities, which can be qualified with categories, linked to properties, and connected through explicit relationships.

Entity-to-entity semantics are organized under qcy:relatedEntity through five top-level relation groups, chosen so that each asserts something different about the pair: qcy:contains (part-whole, transitive), qcy:involves (participation, where the object exists independently of the subject), qcy:follows (order or consequence, transitive, with the later entity as the subject), qcy:expressedBy (anything that is a quality, quantity, time, material or form of the subject) and qcy:interfaces (symmetric; two things that touch, overlap, communicate or work together).

Specific intentions - a signature date, an author, an adjacency - are not sub-properties. They are qcy:RelationCategory instances that name the group they qualify through qcy-t:reifies, and are attached to a particular edge through a qcy:RelationMeta node, which also carries a free-text qcy:description of that instance. A fixed vocabulary of predicates never covers the tail; a group plus a note does.

Categories are managed through qcy:Category and its sub-types: qcy:EntityCategory, qcy:ContentCategory, qcy:MimeCategory, qcy:ProviderType, and qcy:RelationCategory. These are intended as controlled vocabularies for classification and context, and should be extended by adding new SKOS concepts, typically in the qcy-e namespace or in project-specific enum namespaces.

Project-specific specializations are expressed as qcy:RelationCategory instances rather than as new properties, so the set of predicates stays fixed while domain precision grows in the catalogues. A category declares the group it reifies and the entity categories it applies between. The earlier sub-property specializations remain in the ontology as owl:deprecated so that graphs written against them stay readable.

comment.en: A type object rather than an occurrence of one: the IFC type a door instance inherits its shared properties from, written by ifc-processor and pointed at by qcy:inheritsFrom. It is a qcy:EntityMention like any other - it carries a value and categories - but entity resolution never merges a prototype with an occurrence, however alike "Door Type A" and "Door Type A 001" look.

These are standardized representations of named entities that are the output of an enrichment step in the QAECY pipelines. The entity resolution should include relevant contextual information to distinguish between unique named entities. For example, there can be a ground floor in two buildings but they are not the same concept.

A text directive selector specifies a range within a text using the syntax \"#:~:text=[prefix-,]start[,end][,-suffix]\". For example, \"#:~:text=example,fragment\" would indicate a range from the first occurrence of \"example\" to the next occurrence of \"fragment\". This is used to identify the exact location of a qcy:EntityMention within a text fragment.
This special fragment constitutes a page in a paginated document.

The value of an IFC Express ID Selector specifies the ExpressId of the object within the IFC document. Beware that this ID is only unique in context of that single serailization of the model and is likely to change in future versions of the model.
This special fragment constitutes a table with rows and columns. It should specified with a selector (qcy:XYWHSelector) relative to its parent fragment and the qcy:tableGrid should be specified.

comment.undefined: Relationship between either a pair of qcy:EntityMention or qcy:CanonicalEntity occurrences (never between a qcy:EntityMention and a qcy:CanonicalEntity!). This is a general property that should not be used explicitly. Instead, use one of the more specific sub-properties.

comment.en: A file content object represents the full content of a qcy:File. It is uniquely identified by its content, meaning that any modification, even a single character change, results in a new file content object. This ensures that each file content object is immutable and uniquely identifiable. Additionally, a single file content object can be referenced by multiple qcy:File instances, which may be stored in different locations, either locally or in the cloud.
Any quantitative or qualitative property of an entity.

A page selector specifies a particular page within a document. This special selector always always connects a qcy:FileContent object with a qcy:DocumentPage. The value is the page number starting from 1.

comment.undefined: Category derived from the mimetype of the file content

comment.en: A record field selector specifies a named field within a tabular or otherwise keyed record, such as a column of a spreadsheet or a key of a JSON object. The value is the field name as it appears in the record. It records that the selector object was derived from that field, which is what makes it possible to tell afterwards whether a file was described by its name or by a column of a register, and to compare the two.
This special fragment constitutes an image. It should be specified with a selector (qcy:XYWHSelector) relative to its parent fragment and the extracted image's location should be specified.

A selector specifies where in a qcy:InformationObject or a qcy:FileLocation a qcy:EntityReference occurs. For example from/to what index in a text paragraph, what XYWH bounding box on a page, what GlobalId in an IFC file, what range of a file path or what field of a register.

comment.undefined: Category that specifies the role or type of a relationship described by a qcy:RelationMeta node. Instances are SKOS concepts that qualify top-level relationships such as qcy:involves (e.g. Author, Reviewer).

comment.en: A file provider is a source that qcy:FileLocation instances come from, such as one user's computer, a user's browser uploads or a document management system like SharePoint. It is identified within a project by its qcy:remoteProviderId, which every qcy:FileLocation from that source shares, and it carries a human-readable qcy:label and a qcy:providerKind. The same qcy:FileContent can be found at locations from several providers.
The value of an IFC Global ID Selector specifies the GlobalId of the object within the IFC document.
A file location is a digital representation of an information object that is stored on a hard drive, either locally or in the cloud.

The value specifies the bounding box formatted as an xywh box (http://www.w3.org/TR/media-frags/) either in absolute pixels or relative to the information object. The XYWH Selector is used to identify the location of a qcy:EntityMention or qcy:InformationObject within a visual document.

A CAD viewport selector specifies the location of a viewport in a CAD layout. It should be used to connect a qcy:FileContent object representing a CAD layout with a qcy:Fragment representing the viewport. The value is the XYWH coordinates of the viewport within the cartesian coordinate system of the CAD layout (Y axis pointing upwards) normalised to mm. The value corresponds to the window parameter (-w) that is fed to QCAD when extracting an image of the CAD layout and is always.

A document text selector names which text of a document a link was read from, rather than a position within it. The value is the name of that text - for example \"summary\" for a generated summary of the document, or \"text\" for its extracted body text. It is the counterpart of qcy:FilePathSelector and qcy:RecordFieldSelector for claims that come from what a document says rather than from what it is called or how a register lists it, and exists because a match found by scanning a whole document in chunks has no single position that would survive re-extraction.

A text index selector specifies a range within a text using start and end separated by a comma (\"start,end\"). For example \"6,11\" on the text string \"Hello World\" would specify the subset \"World\". This is similar to string slicing in Python and is used to identify the exact location of a qcy:EntityMention within a text fragment.

A CAD layout selector specifies the name of a layout in a CAD file. It should be used to connect a qcy:FileContent object representing a CAD file with a qcy:Fragment representing the layout. The value is the name of the layout as specified in the CAD file and corresponds to the block parameter used when extracting an image of the CAD layout using QCAD.

A file path selector specifies a range within the qcy:filePath of the qcy:FileLocation it is the selector subject of, formatted as start and end separated by a comma (\"start,end\") like qcy:TextIndexSelector. It records that the selector object was derived from that part of the path - typically a classification code a project encodes in its filenames - and is what makes it possible to tell afterwards which segment of which name a link came from.
This special fragment constitutes a CAD layout. It should be specified with a selector (qcy:CADLayoutSelector) relative to its parent fragment and the extracted layout's location should be specified.
The value specifies the time range formatted in accordance with http://www.w3.org/TR/media-frags/
A BIM entity is a special kind of entity mention. It's an intangible (zone) or tangible (element) part of a BIM model.

A coordinate translator specifies the parameters needed to translate coordinates from one coordinate system to another. This is used to connect a qcy:Fragment representing a CAD layout with a qcy:Fragment representing an image of that layout, to enable translation of the viewport coordinates in the CAD layout to XYWH coordinates in the image. The value is formatted as an SVG transformation matrix (eg. matrix(56.69, 0, 0, -56.69, 110.07, 257.10))

comment.undefined: Category derived from the content of the file
Category that specifies the type of provider

comment.en: A fragment is a subset of a qcy:FileContent object. Each fragment can have sub-fragments in any arbitrary depth (see qcy:containsFragment). For example, a page is a fragment of a document and a text paragraph, image, and table can all be sub-fragments of that page.

comment.undefined: A reification node that further qualifies a relationship between two entities. It specifies the subject and object together with a qcy:RelationCategory and optionally the predicate being qualified via qcy:hasRelationMetaProperty. It can qualify any sub-property of qcy:relatedEntity (e.g. qcy:involves, qcy:contains, qcy:leadsTo). This is used when the top-level property alone is insufficient to express the full semantics (e.g. to distinguish that John is the author of drawing A but the reviewer of drawing B).

comment.en: This abstract class captures reference points for all features of interest in a project, such as a building element, a zone, a person, or material. These references can be either explicit or potential occurrences of the entity. This class should not be assigned directly; instead, use the sub-class qcy:EntityMention for potential occurrences of an entity and qcy:CanonicalEntity for a formalized entity.

comment.undefined: Category that specifies the categories of an entity reference

comment.en: This special fragment constitutes a text extraction. It can be the full text of a page a paragraph, footer, header or the like. Except for the former case, it should specified with a selector (qcy:XYWHSelector) to describe it's location relative to its parent fragment. It should also specify a qcy:textRaw and optionally a qcy:textFormatted.

Abstract class for specific categories that each hold enumerations used for specification of information objects and entity references. It is recommended to use SKOS to establish more context between the Category entities.

comment.undefined: Category that specifies what kind of source a qcy:FileProvider is, for example a local device, browser uploads or a document management system.

comment.en: An information object is an abstract class that captures all information found in project files. It can either be the full content of the file (see qcy:FileContent) or a subset (see qcy:Fragment). This abstract class should not be defined explicitly, so instead use one of the more specific sub-classes.

An entity mention is an occurrence of a specific entity within a qcy:InformationObject. Each occurrence is unique, meaning that two mentions of "Albert Einstein" in the same information object are considered two distinct entity mentions. Entity mentions can describe mentionings of persons, organizations, locations, dates, and other proper nouns.

This special fragment constitutes a CAD viewport. It should be specified with a selector (qcy:CADViewportSelector) relative to its parent fragment and the extracted viewport's location should be specified.

The value specifies an identifier within a structured document, such as an XML or JSON file. For BIM models use one of the more specific ID selectors for the specific kind of ID. The ID Selector is typically used to identify the location of a qcy:EntityMention by its unique ID.

extractionPrompt.value: A comes after B, or results from it.

comment.de: Übergeordnete Beziehung, die angibt, dass eine Entität auf eine andere folgt oder aus ihr hervorgeht. Die spätere Entität ist das Subjekt.
comment.it: Relazione di alto livello che indica che un'entità viene dopo un'altra entità, o ne deriva. L'entità successiva è il soggetto.
comment.fr: Relation de haut niveau indiquant qu'une entité vient après une autre entité, ou en résulte. L'entité la plus tardive est le sujet.
comment.da: Overordnet relation der angiver, at en entitet kommer efter eller følger af en anden entitet. Den senere entitet er subjektet.
comment.undefined: Top level relationship that indicates that an entity comes after, or results from, another entity. Written with the later entity as the subject, because at the time a thing is recorded what it followed is known and what will follow it is not.

comment.en: A tag is a keyword or term assigned to a piece of information, such as a qcy:InformationObject, to describe and categorize it. Tags are typically used to facilitate searching and organizing information. An information object can have multiple tags.

comment.undefined: Relationship that specifies that a person or organization is a reviewer of the entity.
Relationship between two information objects where one is an alternative representation of the other. For example an image derived from a PDF page fragment or a CAD drawing.
DEPRECATED: This property is outdated. Please use qcy:adjacentTo instead. Relationship between a zone/element and an adjacent element.

comment.de: Beziehung, die das Startdatum einer Entität in einem Prozesskontext angibt.
comment.it: Relazione che indica la data di inizio di un'entità in un contesto di processo.
comment.fr: Relation qui indique la date de début d'une entité dans un contexte de processus.
comment.da: Relation der angiver startdatoen for en entitet i en proceskontekst.
comment.undefined: Relationship that specifies the start date of an entity in a process context.

comment.en: The file path property specifies the location of a file within its qcy:FileProvider. For a local device it is the absolute path on that machine, normalised to forward slashes (e.g. "/Users/anna/Projects/Nest/A-101.pdf" or "C:/Projects/Nest/A-101.pdf"). For other providers it is the path as the provider presents it.

comment.undefined: Relationship between a qcy:Selector and the thing it specifies. This is typically a qcy:EntityMention (eg this part of the text mentions the entity), a qcy:InformationObject (eg this picture is placed here on the page) or a qcy:CanonicalEntity (eg this part of the file path names this entity).

comment.de: Beziehung, die das Unterzeichnungsdatum einer Entität angibt, z. B. eines Vertrags.
comment.it: Relazione che indica la data di firma di un'entità, ad esempio un contratto.
comment.fr: Relation qui indique la date de signature d'une entité, par exemple un contrat.
comment.da: Relation der angiver underskriftsdatoen for en entitet, f.eks. en kontrakt.
comment.undefined: Relationship that specifies the signature date of an entity such as a contract.

comment.en: The remote relative path specifies the location of a file on a storage system. This is always a relative path in relation to the project directory on a cloud storage provider.
The user id of the person a qcy:FileProvider belongs to, such as the owner of a local device. Not set for shared sources like a document management system.

DEPRECATED: This property is outdated. Please use qcy:contains instead. Relationship that indicates that a building zone contains a building element.

comment.en: The name of the Property Set in the IFC file. Official PSets are considered higher quality and SHACL shapes can be applied to evaluate the BIM model quality.

comment.undefined: DEPRECATED: This property is outdated. Please use qcy:involves instead. The obligation is undertaken by a certain party.

Relationship between a qcy:InformationObject/qcy:FileLocation and a qcy:EntityMention. This property indicates that a file location, file content or fragment mentions a specific named entity. This relationship can implicitly be derived from the subject/object pair of a qcy:Selector. For file locations it is typically resolved by regex mapping of a schema against the file path.
Relationship between a qcy:CanonicalEntity and its geometric representation (for example the SVG polygon org glTF of a BIM object).

Relationship between a qcy:InformationObject and a qcy:Fragment it contains at any depth: one of its own qcy:Fragments, or a qcy:Fragment of one of those. qcy:containsFragment states the direct containment
DEPRECATED: This property is outdated. Please use qcy:contains or qcy:adjacentTo instead. Relationship between a zone and a contained or adjacent element.

comment.en: The number of times resolution has been attempted for this entity mention. Used to limit retry attempts for entity resolution processes. After a maximum number of attempts, the mention is no longer considered for resolution to a canonical entity.

comment.undefined: Relationship that specifies that a person or organization is an author of the entity.
DEPRECATED: This property is outdated. Please use qcy:associatedWith instead. Relationship that specifies the receiving email address of an email file.
DEPRECATED: This property is outdated. Please use qcy:contains instead. Relationship that indicates that a building contains a floor.

comment.de: Beziehung, die angibt, wann eine Entität erstellt wurde.
comment.it: Relazione che indica quando un'entità è stata creata.
comment.fr: Relation qui indique quand une entité a été créée.
comment.da: Relation der angiver, hvornår en entitet blev oprettet.
comment.undefined: Relationship that specifies when an entity was created.

extractionPrompt.value: A 'Schedule' includes an 'Activity'.

comment.undefined: DEPRECATED: This property is outdated. Please use qcy:contains instead. Relationship that specifies that an activity is part of a schedule / project-plan.
Relationship between a qcy:InformationObject and one of its qcy:Fragments

comment.en: The resolved scope a qcy:CanonicalEntity was minted under - the identifiers of its scoping parents, as used in its deterministic identifier. Storey "1" of one building and storey "1" of another are distinct entities carrying the same value, and this is what separates them once they are read back out of the graph: without it a candidate retrieved by similarity carries no scope, and a scope conflict cannot be detected. Empty for categories whose identity does not depend on a containing entity.
Inverse of qcy:mergedInto: the surviving qcy:CanonicalEntity records which entities it absorbed, so a merge can be audited and undone.

comment.undefined: Relationship between an inferred qcy:RelationMeta between two qcy:CanonicalEntity and each of the mention-level qcy:RelationMeta it was derived from. The canonical-level node states that the relationship holds and which qcy:RelationCategory it carries; the mention-level ones it points at hold the evidence — the qcy:description of what in a document established it, its confidence, and through their subject and object the document itself. Written by saturation, never asserted.
Relationship between a qcy:relatedEntity sub-property and one or more formal properties in external ontologies (Ex: qcy:buildingContainsStorey qcy:relatedFormalClass bot:hasStorey).

comment.undefined: DEPRECATED: This property is outdated. Please use qcy:involves instead. Relationship between some activity and required equipment.

comment.undefined: DEPRECATED: This property is outdated. Please use qcy:associatedWith instead. Relationship stating that a person or organization has a role in the contract.

comment.en: The revision of the project schema the document's semantic extraction last ran with. A schema revision newer than this means categories added since were not looked for.

comment.undefined: DEPRECATED: This property is outdated. Please use qcy:contains instead. A drawing sheet contains a drawing entity.

comment.undefined: DEPRECATED: This property is outdated. Please use qcy:contains instead. Relationship that states that the construction project has a project phase.

comment.en: The number of times enrichment has been attempted for this canonical entity. Used to limit retry attempts for enrichment processes (e.g., geocoding addresses). After a maximum number of attempts, the entity is no longer considered for enrichment.

comment.undefined: Relationship between a parent fragment (eg a title) and a child fragment (eg a paragraph).

comment.en: A boolean property specifying that something is explicit. It is specifically used to indicate that a qcy:CanonicalEntity has been confirmed by an authorized project practitioner or other specialist.

A textual explanation or justification supporting an assertion, a piece of data, a derived value, or a relationship. This can include the evidence, logic, or process used to arrive at a conclusion or to assign a confidence score.

extractionPrompt.value: A 'ContractObligation' involves a certain 'ContractCondition'.

comment.undefined: DEPRECATED: This property is outdated. Please use qcy:associatedWith instead. A condition associated with a contract obligation.

extractionPrompt.value: A 'BuildingElement' is made of some 'Material'.

comment.undefined: DEPRECATED: This property is outdated. Please use qcy:expressedBy instead. Relationship between a building element and a material.

Relationship between a qcy:RelationMeta node and the group of qcy:relatedEntity that it qualifies (e.g. qcy:involves, qcy:contains, qcy:follows). DECIDED: nothing emits this. The edge between the subject and the object already names the group, and no consumer reads this property, so writing it would be a second copy of a fact that can go stale. It stays declared because old data may carry it.

comment.en: The 32 character MD5 hash in lower case hexadecimals (empty string = d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e)

extractionPrompt.value: A 'ContractObligation' has a 'Date' that it expires.

comment.undefined: DEPRECATED: This property is outdated. Please use qcy:endsOn instead. The end date of a contract obligation.

Relationship between a qcy:CanonicalEntity and any other representation of the same entity (for example the Wikidata entry) or a similar entity (for example the OpenStreetMaps street address of an appartment in a building). This property indicates that the canonical entity can be linked to or identified with another entity in a different context or dataset.

comment.en: A label is a human-readable name for the resource. Each resource should have only one preferred label in english that specifies the resource.

comment.it: Relazione di alto livello che indica che un'entità coinvolge un'altra entità. Esprime partecipazione o coinvolgimento in un'attività o processo.
comment.fr: Relation de haut niveau indiquant qu'une entité en implique une autre. Elle exprime la participation ou l'engagement dans une activité ou un processus.
comment.da: Overordnet relation der angiver, at en entitet involverer en anden entitet. Den udtrykker deltagelse eller involvering i en aktivitet eller proces.
comment.undefined: Top level relationship that indicates that an entity involves another entity. It expresses a participation or engagement in some activity or process.
DEPRECATED: This property is outdated. Please use qcy:contains instead. Relationship that indicates that a building zone contains a space.

extractionPrompt.value: A 'DrawingSheet' or a 'DrawingEntity' is designed in this 'DrawingScale'.

comment.undefined: DEPRECATED: This property is outdated. Please use qcy:expressedBy instead. Relationship that specifies the scale of a drawing entity or a drawing sheet.

comment.en: The size of the file content in bytes

Text situating a thing in the context it was found in, so that it can be interpreted without returning to the source. On a qcy:EntityMention or qcy:CanonicalEntity this is what distinguishes it from a similarly named one elsewhere - what contains it, which revision or party it belongs to, the role it plays. Written either by a Large Language model at extraction time, where it is kept under ~50 words, or by a processor summarising a source record, where it may be considerably longer. Consumers that feed it to a model should expect the latter and truncate.

comment.undefined: Relationship between an occurrence and the qcy:EntityPrototype it takes its shared properties from - a door instance and its IFC type. Relationship between something and one of its qcy:Properties. Typically a qcy:EntityMention or a qcy:CanonicalEntity, but also a qcy:FileLocation or a qcy:InformationObject: a DMS register records things about a file - its document type, its status, the department that filed it - that are neither entities to resolve nor facts about a file's content, and a qcy:Property holding a label and a value is what those become. Stated with schema:domainIncludes rather than rdfs:domain because qcy:FileLocation, qcy:InformationObject and qcy:EntityReference are pairwise disjoint, so a single rdfs:domain would make every register property an inconsistency - the same reason qcy:mentions, qcy:about and qcy:selectorSubject are stated that way.

This is typically a qcy:InformationObject, but it can also be a qcy:FileLocation - a qcy:FilePathSelector points at a range of that location's qcy:filePath, and a qcy:RecordFieldSelector at the field of a register that described it. Stated with schema:rangeIncludes rather than rdfs:range because qcy:FileLocation and qcy:InformationObject are disjoint, so a single rdfs:range would make every file-location selector an inconsistency.

Inverse of qcy:splitInto: a newly minted qcy:CanonicalEntity records the entity it was separated out of, preserving provenance for a decision that cannot be expressed as a redirect.

A surface form that was judged to denote this qcy:CanonicalEntity but does not normalize to its value - an alias, a translation, an abbreviation. The identifier of a canonical entity is derived from its own normalized value, so a form that merges into it leaves no trace under its own identifier and the cheap identity probe cannot find it again: every later occurrence of that form would be re-adjudicated from scratch, at the same cost, forever. Recording the form here makes the second occurrence free. Values are the same deterministic form identifier the probe computes.
The file suffix including dot (ex: ".pdf")
The operating system of a local device qcy:FileProvider ("darwin", "win32" or "linux"), used to present its qcy:filePath values the way that machine shows them.
